Cow's milk is a bit of a problem to analyze. Studies boast benefits and expose risks in almost equal proportions. I summarize some of my findings here for others to comment on. Note that a lot of studies are either observational, animal-based, or in-vitro. Although these don't definitely prove anything on humans, there's no ethical way to conduct some tests. We can't purposely give people cancer to test our hypothesis. For a lot of things we have to rely on indirect evidence.

  1. IGF-1 is linked to cancer.

    • Harvard University

    • Diet, IGF-1 and cancer risk

    • I don't find studies that contradict IGF-1's involvement in cancer growth, although some find that serum levels of IGF-1 alone may not be a strong predictor. For example, expressing IGF-1 as a ratio with IGFBP-3 produces a stronger predictor.

    • exercise mitigates the risk as the IGF-1 levels are significantly lower in athletes than sedentary people.

    • IGF-1 is also found in meats, but if I'm looking to reduce my consumption of it without becoming a vegan, dairy is an easier way to do this than removing meat (for me). I've also reduced my meat consumption to about 6oz per day or less because of this.

    • Milk consumption and fractures. Sampling studies out there recorded in reputable journals yields a mixed bag of results.

      • Milk consumption not correlated with fewer fractures.

      • Osteoporosis higher in countries that consume more milk - given industrialized western nations drink more milk than others.

      • However, higher consumption of milk during childhood may prevent osteoporosis in adulthood.

      • Risk of osteoporosis decreased by Vitamin D consumption along with calcium

      • Calcium supplementation does not help bone density

  3. Milk consumption and cardiovascular disease (CVD).

    • Milk consumption may be inversely associated with overall CVD risk

    • Milk and Dairy don't correlate to CVD nor Diabetes

    • All recent studies I see exonerate milk specifically. I don't see studies in peer reviewed publications that conclude the opposite.. However, Calcium intake increases risk of CVD

  4. D-galactose found in milk is an inflammatory.

    • In Rats

    • Mentioned as an inflammatory

    • Causes aging and neurological damage in mice

    • I find no studies implicating ill effects of D-galactose on humans directly, but this is one of those things that is hard to ethically test on humans so we rely on things like animal studies to help along the way.

  5. Milk and bone growth. Another mixed bag.

    • Neither milk nor calcium intake appears to have any beneficial effect on children's bones according to these review studies: [1] [2]. However, these studies were not published in more reputable journals and I mostly see them in pro-vegan sites. Plenty of studies like this one and this one contradict those findings.

    • Cow-milk, soy-milk, and human milk yielded similar bone mineral content in children up to 1 year old

    • Children who avoid drinking cow milk have low dietary calcium intakes and poor bone health

    • Milk enhanced bone mineral accretion

  6. It's a FODMAP, many people are lactose intollerant

    • Although identifying lactose intolerance is straight-forward, identifying triggers for functional gastrointestinal disorders is not. Milk is a FODMAP because of the galactans that although might not cause inflammation and other problems, might be a trigger to such conditions as Cron's disease.

  7. Milk and all disease observational studies. Some of these are concerning.

    • High milk consumption in early childhood linked to diabetes

    • Milk consumption linked to prostate cancer

    • Milk consumption associated with various cancers

    • Milk consumption associated with cancers of the lymphatic organs

    • Milk and iron deficiency

    • Milk and breast cancer risk unclear

  8. Conclusions:

    • The benefits outweigh the risks

    • Limit or eliminate in babies and toddlers

    • Eliminate in infants

    • Me: easy enough to stay away from milk so I'll keep doing so. Hard cheeses occasionally may be fine since they have lower doses of some of the more dangerous aspects of milk (like IGF-1).

A few days ago I had a conversation with Thidran and we discussed a number of interesting topics surrounding GamerGate. For those of you who don't know, Thidran is the owner of the Burgers & Fries IRC channel and imageboard. Thidran has been a key player in GamerGate since the beginning and in our conversation he tells the (from his perspective) 'true story' of how GamerGate began.

Here is the full conversation: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ib28t5jkxtI

Here are some of the key things discussed:

  • GamerGate isn't only about ethics in gaming journalism. GamerGate is about improving the industry as a whole.

  • GamerGate needs to focus more on digging, individual projects and industry issues.

  • Thidran condemns the threats the threats the LWs have received and he opposes doxxing.

  • Burgers & Fries was always concerned with ethics, people on both sides need to stop claiming that they weren't.

  • Gamers should form a Wikileaks-esque site where game developers can anonymously report on alleged abuses by publishers and studios.

  • Leigh Alexander was right in her list about all of the problems in the gaming industry. Gamers should reach out to (moderates in) the SJW crowd and work towards common goals.

  • GamerGate isn't a movement, it's an ongoing event (similar to a war).

  • GamerGate is actually a proxy war between channers and Something Awful goons.

  • Discussion of the Zoe Post didn't start on 4chan, it actually started on Something Awful and Penny Arcade.

  • Burgers & Fries was separate from GamerGate, but some bad things did happen during the Burgers & Fries era.

  • The reason some people focused on Zoe Quinn during the Burgers & Fries era is because of her attacks on the chans and her long history with Something Awful. Another reason is because early on The Fine Young Capitalists went public about Quinn's harassment and DDoS campaign against them and because CameraLady's digging revealed her ties with Silverstring Media and the IGF.

  • Thidran alleges that he has evidence showing that Zoe Quinn's friends are responsible for much of her alleged harassment. Also alleges that Zoe Quinn personally reached out to journalists in order to push her "gamers are harassing me" narrative.

  • Thidran alleges that Alex Lifschitz (billionaire playboy who opposes GamerGate) is manipulating the SJW crowd for his own personal ends.

  • Thidran called out some of the alleged "bad actors" on his side. He alleges that The Ralph and Neirdan have behaved unethically. Referred to Robin Gething as "an idiot."

  • Thidran believes the 4chan censorship of GamerGate was because the 4chan moderators lost their cool and received too many false reports, causing them to nuke everything.

What do you guys think of the topics discussed? Do you think Thidran's timeline of events is accurate? Should GamerGate focus more on industry issues? Should gamers form a Wikileaks-esque website to help game developers go public with industry abuses?

Is Thidran right about GamerGate actually being a proxy war between channers and SA goons? If GamerGate is indeed actually a conflict between channers and goons, what does that mean for both sides? Did Zoe Quinn and her friends craft the harassment narrative themselves? Is GamerGate an event, rather than a movement? Are you glad to see that Thidran condemned threats/doxxing and even called out some of the alleged "bad actors" on the "pro-gamer" side?
[Discussion] What do you think of the points Thidran brought up?
